config.theme: Incident postmortem: the checkout outage last Tuesday
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Incident postmortem: the checkout outage last Tuesday

personas.name: Tess
personas.goals: Real fixes before the next big on-sale
personas.hidden_agenda: Her team pushed the CDN change

personas.name: Jonas
personas.role: Network engineer who made the CDN change
personas.hidden_agenda: Was told the change was routine and low-risk

personas.name: Delphine
personas.role: Head of partnerships, owns the promoter relationship
personas.hidden_agenda: The promoter's CEO called her personally, furious

agenda.title: Why
agenda.goal: Understand the CDN change and the bot traffic

agenda.title: Before the next on-sale
agenda.goal: What must be true before March 21

facts.statement: Bot traffic share during the on-sale = 70%
The CDN rule change went live at 9:41 am
Reviewers on the CDN rule change = 0

beats.summary: The sequence; Tess undercounts the duration
The rule change and the bots; Jonas's bot share is low and is corrected
Customers, refunds and the promoter; Delphine's penalty figure is inflated; Kwesi's double-charge count goes uncorrected

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Let's keep this blameless. Kwesi, you were on call. What did you see?

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: The on-sale opened at ten. Within a minute the checkout pages were timing out.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: Within a minute. On the biggest on-sale of the year.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: And we were down for about half an hour before it recovered.

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: It was longer than that. The graphs say fifty-two minutes.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Fifty-two. You're right. I was thinking of when we found the cause.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: How many tickets did we sell before it fell over?

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: Thirty-one hundred. Out of eighteen thousand.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: Thirty-one hundred. The promoter has the same graph.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: What fixed it in the end?

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: Rolling back the CDN rule. Once the old rule was back, the queue started working.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: The CDN rule. That nobody reviewed.

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: It wasn't reviewed, no.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Why. Jonas, what was the change?

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: A rule to cache the event pages more aggressively. It went live at nine forty-one.

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: Nineteen minutes before the on-sale.

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: It was meant to help with load. It had the opposite effect on the queue tokens.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Who reviewed it?

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: Nobody. CDN rules don't go through review. They never have.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: That's insane. Sorry, it is.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: It's a gap. Let's call it a gap.

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: The other thing is the bots. Maybe a third of the traffic was bots.

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: The security dashboard has seventy percent. Seventy percent of requests were bots.

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: Seventy. Okay. That changes things.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: So real fans were fighting robots for tickets, and then the site died.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Did the queue system hit its limit?

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: Not even close. It's built for forty thousand concurrent users. The CDN rule broke it before it got there.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: My daughter tried to buy tickets for this concert. She got the error page eleven times.

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: She wasn't the only one. My cousin did too.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: She's fourteen. She thinks I work for the worst company on earth.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Okay. From now on, CDN rule changes need a second reviewer and can't go out within two hours of an on-sale.

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: That's fair. I'll write the review rule into the deploy pipeline this week.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: The fallout. Delphine, the promoter.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: The promoter is threatening the penalty clause. That's a hundred thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: I have the contract summary here. The penalty clause is fifty thousand.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: Fifty. Fine. It's still fifty thousand dollars and a relationship.

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: And some people got charged twice. Maybe fifty customers.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Have they been refunded?

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: Not yet. Finance needs a list.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: Customer service got sixty-eight hundred emails. People are angry.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Could someone get finance the double-charge list today?

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: I'll pull the list and send it to finance before lunch.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: Can we give the promoter something? A fee waiver, a statement, anything?

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: A public statement that says it was our fault, not theirs, would help.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Then we waive our booking fee on this event, and we put out a statement taking responsibility.

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: I'll draft the statement with comms and show it to the promoter first.

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: Does legal need to see the statement before it goes out?

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: Who's going to answer the sixty-eight hundred emails?

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: Support is doing a single reply to all of them, with the refund details.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Last. The next big on-sale is March twenty-first. What has to be true by then?

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: The review rule, and a freeze on CDN changes during on-sales.

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: And bot protection. Seventy percent bots means real fans can't get in.

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: Do we even know whose bots they were?

turns.speaker: Delphine
turns.text: Maybe we try a verified-fan presale, like the bigger companies do.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Let's look at what verified-fan would take before committing to it.

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: It'd be worth someone talking to the CDN vendor about their bot product.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Jonas, could you set up that call with the vendor?

turns.speaker: Jonas
turns.text: Yes. This week.

turns.speaker: Tess
turns.text: Thank you, everyone. Get some sleep, Kwesi.

turns.speaker: Kwesi
turns.text: Working on it.
